|
# [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138695955/644885942/-1343999874?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTVjNmEyNzUtMTRhYS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FJfFnbGPVyBYbFEMcY0Wwm7m6ikm0Uai-IWLMLnNydI=)
Happy Labor Day weekend, Peter.

Before I ran for Congress, I was a member of United Auto Workers Local 4811, working alongside my family at our auto shop in Bakersfield. I learned what it means to organize, to look out for the person next to you, and to fight for a fair shake, long before I ever thought about running for office.

So it means everything to me that UAW has officially endorsed this campaign, with local members stepping up to knock doors and make calls to help us win our primary in June — and that support hasn't slowed down since.

The UAW isn't the only union standing with us. I'm proud to have the support of the United Farm Workers, National Nurses United and the California Teachers Association.
[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138695957/644885944/1981932151?refcode=em-9.6.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTVjNmEyNzUtMTRhYS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FJfFnbGPVyBYbFEMcY0Wwm7m6ikm0Uai-IWLMLnNydI=)_Rallying alongside United Farm Workers in Bakersfield_
Unions know what families in this district are up against right now, because Valadao and this administration have made life harder for the people who keep the Central Valley running.

That's the choice in this race. Valadao takes money from corporate interests, and that's who he works for. I've never taken a dollar of corporate PAC money, and never will. The only endorsements I'm chasing are the ones from the people who actually do the work.

This Labor Day, I just want to say thank you. To every union member who's knocked a door for this campaign, made a call, or shown up to a canvass launch. This has never been about one person. It's about all of us.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138695959/644885947/1981932151?refcode=em-9.6.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTVjNmEyNzUtMTRhYS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FJfFnbGPVyBYbFEMcY0Wwm7m6ikm0Uai-IWLMLnNydI=)
In Solidarity,
Randy | [Donate ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138695962/644885949/1981932151?refcode=em-9.6.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTVjNmEyNzUtMTRhYS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FJfFnbGPVyBYbFEMcY0Wwm7m6ikm0Uai-IWLMLnNydI=)

I learned what it means to organize, to look out for the person next to you, and to fight for a fair shake, long before I ever thought about running for office. The UAW isn't the only union standing with us. I'm proud to have the support of the United Farm Workers, National Nurses United and the California Teachers Association. alongside United Farm Workers in Bakersfield Unions know what families in this district are up against right now, because Valadao and this administration have made life harder for the people who keep the Central Valley running. Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton win the U.S. Senate race in Texas. "We in the Senate don't have the money budgeted for Texas. We need help from the president," said Senator John Kennedy (R-LA). Republican Leader John Thune (R-SD) later confirmed the plan to abandon Paxton financially and deflected responsibility to the president. "I'm hoping the White House will become engaged; Texas is an incredibly expensive state," Thune said. What makes this so infuriating is that the Senate GOP spent over $100 million attacking Ken Paxton in the Republican primary. **They had plenty of money to spend on Texas when they were trying to defeat a conservative, but when it comes to defeating a Marxist like James Talarico, they’ve got nothing.** You would think that since they spent so much against the party's eventual nominee, they would feel some obligation to help him now. **This race is competitive because they hurt Paxton in the primary. It should be on them, not President Trump, to clean up their mess. You break it, you own it.** Sadly, that's not going to happen. You may hear party leaders say they "hope" Ken Paxton wins and they "hope" President Trump helps him, but they have closed their wallets and are quietly rooting for him to lose. They don't want another conservative in the Senate who will hold them accountable, and they would love to tell everyone that Ken Paxton was a bad candidate who cost them the majority, even though they're the ones who kneecapped and left him for dead. **TAKE ACTION** **Conservatives are right to be mad about this, but being mad won't change it. Reflecting on Labor Day| | | |
---
| | | I got to spend some time on the water this week, and it didn’t come without a lot of reflection. **This Labor Day weekend, I’m thinking about the monumental shift in how we treat workers and labor as corporate leaders chart a course to replace humans with AI. ** We have a roadmap for protecting people, in the history of our country's labor movement. Workers didn't wait for permission when factories chewed through twelve-hour shifts every single day -- they organized, they walked off the job, and they built the eight-hour day, the weekend, and the basic idea that people deserve a say in how new technology gets used in our society. That fight for working people is exactly what built the middle class in Northern Wisconsin. And, I realize it’s the work and sacrifice of the organizers and labor leaders before us that afforded all of us the right to enjoy long weekends like Labor Day with families and friends indoors, outdoors, or out on the water.Basic human dignity, the right to work, and the right to rest is worth fighting for. Have a wonderful (and restful) Labor Day.

Fred

(Here's a photo of me on the water)

##### Read this one. Putin built himself a fleet of a thousand ghost ships that no court on earth can touch. They earn him more than the entire West has sent Ukraine since the tanks rolled in, and a lot of them keep parking on top of the undersea cables that carry your money across the ocean.
##### Nobody has ever proven why. That's the design, and Lawrence lays out how it got built and who decided it wasn't worth stopping. [Paid subscribers get all of it](https://substack.com/redirect/e18063ac-42e1-4364-b789-67bc0d6f7bd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). * * *
_**by Lawrence Winnerman**_
I have been listening to and reading [Olga Lautman](https://open.substack.com/users/33996559-olga-lautman?utm_source=mentions) and [Julie Roginsky](https://open.substack.com/users/36550640-julie-roginsky?utm_source=mentions) since I joined Substack, and for most of that time I have been skating past the same two words--_shadow fleet_. Every time I heard it, I nodded along, filed it under things I would look up later, and went back to whatever I was doing.
Last week after Cliff hosted Olga and [Jacob Kaarsbo](https://open.substack.com/users/361212155-jacob-kaarsbo?utm_source=mentions) for _**World War NEXT**_ , I finally looked it up. I want to tell you what I found, because I spent 25 years inside large, complicated, heavily regulated systems, and I did not know a thing like this was possible.
There are somewhere between 800 and 1,200 oil tankers at sea right now that do not, in any way a court can use, have a country.
I understood sanctions evasion in the abstract, the way everyone does, from Tom Clancy novels, or TV or the movies. Somebody swaps a label, somebody routes a payment through Dubai, somebody looks away. Cash changes hands, or these days, maybe bitcoin. What I did not understand is that the entire legal architecture of the ocean rests on one thing, and that thing is the flag a ship claims to fly, and that a flag is a product with a price.
## What The Shadow Fleet Actually Is
In December 2022, the European Union embargoed seaborne Russian crude and the G7 imposed a price cap. The cap was a clever piece of design, and it resulted in everything that follows. It did not try to stop Russian oil, because stopping Russian oil would have spiked pump prices in an election year, and god forbid that happen. It said instead that Western companies could ship, insure, and finance Russian oil only if that oil sold at or below a set price, starting at $60 a barrel. Russia could sell its oil, it just couldn't really profit from it. Neato.
Russia's answer to this was to stop using Western companies--at all.
Over the next 3 years Moscow and its buyers assembled a parallel merchant fleet: old tankers nearing the end of their useful lives bought near scrap value, registered in countries that do not ask questions, insured by Russian firms or by nobody, owned on paper by shell companies in Dubai and Hong Kong that dissolve and reappear.
The Kyiv School of Economics, which counts the ships that actually load, found 176 shadow tankers lifting Russian crude and products in June of this year, 54% of all loadings that month. Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Ukraine's presidential commissioner for sanctions, put the core at 400 vessels that have made 3 or more voyages from Russian ports since 2024, inside a wider range of 800 to 1,200. The European Union has now sanctioned 673 individual ships by name, with more every week.
They keep sailing, and the list of ships keeps getting bigger.

## The Ghost Ships
Ninety-four percent of the tankers KSE tracked in June were more than 15 years old. A tanker's working life runs about 20 to 25 years, after which insurers and classification societies push it toward the breakers in Bangladesh or Pakistan. The walking dead of ships, so to speak. The shadow fleet is, to a real extent, the global scrap pool bought back and put to sea, and roughly 60% of it carries no insurance any Western underwriter would recognize. One in 3 tanker transits in the Baltic now runs on Russian paper, which may or may not be worth anything at all.
Then there are the flags. A ship's flag state is the government legally responsible for it, and small countries have sold that responsibility as a revenue line for a century. Cameroon, Sierra Leone, Gabon, Comoros, and Equatorial Guinea are all in heavy rotation. The maritime intelligence firm Windward has identified 23 countries whose flags are being flown through fraudulent registries the International Maritime Organization does not recognize at all, including Syria, Eritrea, and Myanmar.
In May, Cameroon threw 38 sanctioned tankers off its registry and notified the IMO in writing that it had done so. Twenty-four of them are still broadcasting the Cameroonian flag.
And it gets stranger. Mongolia, the second-largest landlocked country on earth, operates a flag with about 3,000 ships on it, administered by a for-profit company in Singapore that employs somewhere between 11 and 50 people. Bolivia has had no coastline since Chile took it in 1884 and runs a registry anyway. But the countries that do not run registries are the more instructive half.
In February the International Maritime Organization counted 529 vessels worldwide flying false flags, and among the flags being flown were Malawi's, Mali's, Botswana's, and Lesotho's. Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa. It has no coast, no port, and no river access to the sea, and it has had to formally notify the IMO that it does not operate a ship registry, because certificates in its name somehow kept turning up on ships.
The best case is Eswatini, which is landlocked, is not an IMO member, and has never operated a registry at all. In late 2023 an Indian firm stood one up out of Singapore anyway, and inside 3 months there were 364 vessels on its books, the 3 largest of them tied to Syrian sanctions violations and to allegedly stolen Ukrainian grain. In April 2024 the IMO gave up and designated every ship claiming that flag as "False Eswatini."
Cameroon at least had a registry to throw those 38 tankers off of. Eswatini never sold anything. Somebody built a website, and no one really knows who.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e18063ac-42e1-4364-b789-67bc0d6f7bd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

## The Money
The Center for Strategic and International Studies estimates that the shadow fleet carries about 65% of Russia's seaborne oil, roughly 3.7 million barrels a day, worth $87 to $100 billion a year. That is more money than the entire West has sent Ukraine since the tanks crossed the border in February 2022.
The price cap now sits at $44.10 a barrel, frozen there for a year by the EU's July sanctions package so that a war-driven price spike would not lift it automatically. Urals crude sold at about $60 in July. The gap between those two numbers, multiplied by 3.7 million barrels a day, is the entire point of this business. China took 36% of shadow fleet cargoes in June and India took 18%. The destination of the remaining 40% is logged as unknown. Just--unknown. Poof!
Forty percent of a hundred-billion-dollar trade goes somewhere nobody is writing down. I would like to know who is not looking, and why, please.
## Then I Got to the Part About the Cables
Ninety-nine percent of international data moves through fiber-optic cables lying on the ocean floor. Not satellites. Cables, roughly the diameter of a garden hose in deep water, carrying the internet, interbank settlement, and military traffic between continents.
On Christmas Day 2024, a tanker called the _Eagle S_ , flying the flag of the Cook Islands, "accidentally" dragged its anchor about 90 kilometers across the floor of the Gulf of Finland. It severed the EstLink 2 power cable between Finland and Estonia and 4 data cables along with it. Repairs took 7 months. In October 2025 a Finnish district court threw the criminal case out for lack of jurisdiction, on the theory that the damage happened outside Finnish territorial waters and belonged to the crew's home countries or to the Cook Islands. On August 27 of this year, the Helsinki Court of Appeal reversed that and ruled that cutting a cable is not a maritime accident under the law of the sea. The case goes back to trial.
It was not the first. In October 2023 a Chinese-owned vessel named _Newnew Polar Bear_ , outbound from a Russian port, dragged an anchor more than 100 nautical miles and broke the Balticconnector gas pipeline. Four Baltic cables have been damaged since the beginning of 2025. In May of that year Polish aircraft chased off a tanker that was circling the SwePol power cable.
No investigation has ever established intent. Not one.

body:
An issue a day

| |
---
| | _With just two days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 2, I am highlighting the need to make sure Granite Staters can afford to live in the place they call home._
* * *
Dear David, We’re facing a nationwide housing crisis. And with our regressive property tax system, Granite Staters are really feeling it, especially in our mobile home parks. Many retirees move into manufactured housing and mobile home parks thinking that they’ve found an affordable place to enjoy their well-deserved retirement. But land rent and lot fees keep skyrocketing because out-of-state companies backed by private equity are buying up the parks and raising the price residents pay for the land under their homes. This, in turn, is exacerbated by the cost-of-living crisis and constant downshifting our cash-strapped municipalities are facing and why property taxes are also going up. Now, we have residents who purchased mobile homes and have seen the land rent go up by hundreds of dollars a month at the same time as their property taxes have gone up by hundreds of dollars a month. If you’re living on a fixed income, you can’t absorb those huge increases. **[More of the same won’t fix this. Before I tell you how I plan to fix it, can you pitch in today to help me take this fight to Congress?](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/Ns4tJOBL3hLQnB6Hf81Nlg~~/AAUS1hA~/1iMy1jcFgHUNZEYM58C1GUzizNNqbB-JM91gDf92ACfQLM8mfXcqHK4cWvjMt_RfA96rN3bFxywjeNDd-a7Z8YI3STkj3lAFiKM0EpGtUSUNSFRDYmxao0P3q-kUKiNYNI9TgJkfABKno_oQhT8j9AwM4pPLeMNXzJ5hnTCgQIuIEl_ahxoDvdnzaGDhj3sMw1uCm-ZvLrmP4aWysashmUMIZvrk4OOgJ4p3C97_16HPRed8eAvk22-IwOuIuxdEf2M5GlDZ7zSwVy1hIjPe-A~~)** | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/Ns4tJOBL3hLQnB6Hf81Nlg~~/AAUS1hA~/1iMy1jcFgHUNZEYM58C1GUzizNNqbB-JM91gDf92ACfQLM8mfXcqHK4cWvjMt_RfA96rN3bFxywjeNDd-a7Z8YI3STkj3lAFiKM0EpGtUSUNSFRDYmxao0P3q-kUKiNYNI9TgJkfABKno_oQhT8j9AwM4pPLeMNXzJ5hnTCgQIuIEl_ahxoDvdnzaGDhj3sMw1uCm-ZvLrmP4aWysashmUMIZvrk4OOgJ4p3C97_16HPRed8eAvk22-IwOuIuxdEf2M5GlDZ7zSwVy1hIjPe-A~~)

**People like Sue, Tom, and the hundreds of other Granite Staters who have told me they can’t afford to stay in their manufactured housing deserve a leader who fights to ensure they can.** That’s why I also released my plan to stop these increases and support residents seeking to purchase their parks and form cooperatives.
**[You can read more about it here on my website, but here’s a quick summary of what I’ll fight for in Congress:](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/X3se7_HhTaX0UeaKyDoh9Q~~/AAUS1hA~/wgSnZMPkncspL4x78KmdPmM3ozWMb54yr9GyHB_racks9dUvvVN88L12WmbWxdUlkPkrC1YkGcc1q129KP1u7n9XPKdU2crwq3IMoynqL36JZnqM9Auc_15wPGNpfpmStYCwZLZAVogBuxIHSRE7hjpvpLJaoXffUtyGhOCl8Ewe-gjJ3FW33aLwgHBMHB3l_K4HwzavfQ8zCeTqVpHzMOeJ_D7l3eZF8TsyBjjfx6I~)**
* I will help push for the Manufactured Housing Community Sustainability Act in Congress, which would forgive 75 percent of the capital gains tax when a park is sold to a resident cooperative instead of another investor.
* I will support the Promoting Residential Ownership of Manufactured Home Communities Act, introduced by Rep. Maxwell Frost in March, which pushes states to strengthen their opportunity-to-purchase laws (we helped pioneer this in NH in the 1980s and need to catch back up) and helps residents with down payment assistance.
* I will put federal money behind cooperatives so their residents’ offer is as good as cash. This is what our own New Hampshire Community Loan Fund was built to do, and it is why 152 communities here are resident-owned and 9,000 homes have stayed affordable.

**[We all deserve to be able to retire, and we all deserve to be able to afford the places we want to call home when we do. For Day 2, I am highlighting the need to make sure Granite Staters can afford to live in the place they call home. Dear David, We’re facing a nationwide housing crisis. And with our regressive property tax system, Granite Staters are really feeling it, especially in our mobile home parks. Many retirees move into manufactured housing and mobile home parks thinking that they’ve found an affordable place to enjoy their well-deserved retirement. But land rent and lot fees keep skyrocketing because out-of-state companies backed by private equity are buying up the parks and raising the price residents pay for the land under their homes. This, in turn, is exacerbated by the cost-of-living crisis and constant downshifting our cash-strapped municipalities are facing and why property taxes are also going up. Now, we have residents who purchased mobile homes and have seen the land rent go up by hundreds of dollars a month at the same time as their property taxes have gone up by hundreds of dollars a month. If you’re living on a fixed income, you can’t absorb those huge increases. ~~ | | ~~ On Thursday, I held a press conference to bring attention to this issue and highlight the stories of people like Sue and Tom who have personally been affected by rising rents. | People like Sue, Tom, and the hundreds of other Granite Staters who have told me they can’t afford to stay in their manufactured housing deserve a leader who fights to ensure they can. That’s why I also released my plan to stop these increases and support residents seeking to purchase their parks and form cooperatives. ~ I will help push for the Manufactured Housing Community Sustainability Act in Congress, which would forgive 75 percent of the capital gains tax when a park is sold to a resident cooperative instead of another investor. I will support the Promoting Residential Ownership of Manufactured Home Communities Act, introduced by Rep. Maxwell Frost in March, which pushes states to strengthen their opportunity-to-purchase laws (we helped pioneer this in NH in the 1980s and need to catch back up) and helps residents with down payment assistance. I will put federal money behind cooperatives so their residents’ offer is as good as cash. This is what our own New Hampshire Community Loan Fund was built to do, and it is why 152 communities here are resident-owned and 9,000 homes have stayed affordable. ~~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: ** | - | | ~~ Thank you, Carleigh | Carleigh Beriont is running to represent New Hampshire’s First Congressional District in Congress because Granite Staters deserve a representative who shows up and listens. ~~** | | ~~ | Paid for by Carleigh Beriont for Congress Carleigh Beriont for CongressPO Box 1912Hampton, NH 03843United States "Website"•~~ "Privacy Policy"

Working cows and driving tractors growing up made me who I am today. It taught me the value of hard work, the importance of keeping your word, and what it means to sacrifice for something bigger than yourself. Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. I didn't come to Washington because I love asking true patriots like you for money. I didn't run for Congress at 29 years old to become the youngest House Republican so I could spend my nights begging for donations. I came because my kids deserve to grow up in a better America than I grew up in — and right now, that's not guaranteed. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father Almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. I refuse to look my kids in the eye someday and tell them I gave up when it mattered most. [**That's why I'm still here. That's why I keep sending these messages.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/rvmiEj3p1FFUR-dnCaPpT3hX-mxcOR0JrYu6YtpES9SrkDultga06N3vStFvvaJrlhlNcvPzzskawrDSr-TT1uO79IW3vOLt2xnPt5gALBJg0E7ZJ-ipE-5EdiB4JyOWtiHFLfxKYgSETl8kXEXb1Hw3TDL0oz1m8JuX3EP6HfsddqTaifC1dZPZAmRJWIw_JpCsPr7fGSZu5oOfCiCYVHBQSsH9hU29sU4A-6J_ywqFN1GOf9z_toV5uHSUvF4YlPzImQFnsVI2d1Le98mgFRhelVZNofS8lFKulkHft4rB8W4va7UGMWKrrbGJBlJEpg4nRYsOvRAxMrHgAZYGhJVP7i9_wGeN_6T9FT46SS25P7ECLr0j45zIZspO-xIqkaOR5et1TCOrK2WOWkiU5omkB75NIXRfjRxKY4kNwCe3Jp4jaRE7HzTBU7h7tAZfJWn3cjHlNZHAk0fMqvLpVOFju9rFjjX7rOcrr0m9fu8LqOUUs-3KUKa4D0K55ftv6Gw1K4dOPLcD88oO_AHOnqqLslZZ1QfxYsX6zEf3WUZhoNNdPij25dbqD71JjJWWwgX2ntZM8AU9Jw1yPoLbR_JbvjqELls4EpNTUeKf6vW465Qp_bVfyIfsy5lPslXfvqBq8Xn4lv2aZBeQetHIlY4VZMbJCdnnQLY3v6O5BRun4pmjgnYjpk2dkE7osKBJ5Em0hrbbw4UJGRl07yy3ms7ndm72aYpVAeNIFR1gVdw3i9YJrq5EXW-lUnK_ORjsulvWOt0miIdkm0U1zepq_OnITioSo0DmkLRs4aJafF488DvlqV1toTsQV3ezgPEEFWUR_BQ/6Wjmgk23WToh18LCMJ1pLau_prqZjV6N/24) Because nothing — I repeat — nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country. The left hates you. They hate your vote. They hate MAGA for putting America First. And they will do anything — lie, cheat, steal, destroy — to ensure your children inherit a country you won't even recognize. Peter, today I'll make the same promise to you that I've made to myself, to my wife, and to my children: As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. Folks,
In 2010, I ran for Nevada State Senate and lost to the Republican incumbent by about 20 points.
I could’ve easily given up, but I didn’t. I kept fighting. I got back up, ran again in 2012, won, and eventually became Senate Majority Leader.
Fast forward to 2022, I ran for reelection as Attorney General and won by the largest margin of any statewide candidate in Nevada that year.

So yes, the polls in this race are close. But you and I both know MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo is running scared. He's banking on billionaire money to dominate the airwaves and prop up his campaign because he can't win over voters on his failed record.

subject: Priorities

body:
The establishment tells us that there’s only one path to winning: _Don’t upset the status quo, don’t take on the concentration of greed taking over our country, and instead spend most of your time fundraising from powerful donors._
But this campaign didn’t win in 2018 by following the establishment playbook. We won, together, through organizing and building a movement of working class voices that went unheard in our politics for far too long.
I’m not going to change my priorities or how I campaign. But that means I’m counting on grassroots supporters like you to fund this campaign — not wealthy donors cutting big checks at fancy fundraisers.
If I can count on your support, chip in any amount that makes sense to you toward my re-election campaign today:

name: Roy Cooper
subject: re: my decision
body:
I can’t do this alone, Peter.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1291&source=&t=1&akid=3198%2E124072%2E6InhYE) | | | |
---
Peter, I’m in a bit of a bind.
A recent poll shows that our race is now statistically tied, and the Senate GOP’s top super PACs are currently outspending us to boost my Republican opponent. That’s because Senate control hinges on this battleground race.
Since I’m running a grassroots campaign, I can’t fight back without you. So if you’re able to chip in a few bucks to power our fight today, I’d really appreciate it. Here’s the link to donate:
[**_https:/actblue.com/donate_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1291&amount=5&t=8&akid=3198%2E124072%2E6InhYE)
Now, my decision to run for Senate wasn’t made lightly.
Serving as Governor was one of the great experiences of my life, but after my second term, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie. From adding hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs to giving school teachers much-needed raises to expanding access to Medicaid, **my #1 priority was to improve the lives of everyday people – and we did that.**
That’s why it’s so upsetting to see how Washington DC insiders have turned their backs on hardworking people. Insiders like Michael Whatley, my opponent in this race.
My opponent says he’ll lower costs, but he built his career promoting the interests of Big Oil and utility companies at the expense of working families. He says he’ll protect our communities, but as chair of the state GOP, he appointed a convicted child sex offender who served six years in prison to powerful leadership roles within the party because he could raise money. He claims he’ll fight for North Carolinians, but it’s clear that **_his_ priority is choosing himself and his wealthy friends.**
_It’s no wonder why the President anointed him to run after Thom Tillis bowed out of running for this seat._
So while I didn’t plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn’t stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut resources for public education and chip away at the middle class. They are not making this country “great again.”
I had to get back in the fight, and I’m so glad I did.
Ever since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side.
The hard part will be maintaining it for the next nine weeks or so left in this race.
Republicans are spending nearly $100 million so far to turn voters against me and save their Senate majority – and this surge of dark money is taking a toll on our narrow polling lead.
We can fight back and win in North Carolina, but just as in elections past, I can’t do it alone.
**[_Please, Peter – will you chip in what you can today to help me flip this seat, retake the Senate for Democrats and return power in Washington DC to the hands of working families?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1291&amount=5&t=9&akid=3198%2E124072%2E6InhYE)**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1291&amount=5&t=10&akid=3198%2E124072%2E6InhYE)

Thanks for being on this team.
Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1291&source=&t=3&akid=3198%2E124072%2E6InhYE)

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: I’ll never stop fighting for our right to vote
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
SCOTUS just cleared the way for Trump’s attacks on mail-in voting.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260906-6692-footer&t=1&akid=6692%2E420207%2Ey2q9Ac)
I'm furious, Peter.
Trump has spent this entire election cycle attacking vote-by-mail — a method that over a third of Americans use — to restrict who can receive mail-in ballots.
**And last week, the Supreme Court cleared the way for him to continue gutting mail-in voting protections.**
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260906.YKe_7u&refcode=em20260906-6692&t=2&akid=6692%2E420207%2Ey2q9Ac) [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260906.YKe_7u&refcode=em20260906-6692&t=3&akid=6692%2E420207%2Ey2q9Ac)
It’s two months before the midterms. Ballots are already on their way to voters' mailboxes in some states.
**This is completely unacceptable. It’s authoritarian overreach, plain and simple.**
Peter, mail-in voting is safe, secure, and has been used by millions of Americans for generations. Contrary to the falsehoods this administration is peddling, there is no evidence of widespread fraud in our mail-in voting system. Period.
**Let’s be clear on what this is really about: Trump doesn’t hate mail-in voting because he’s concerned about the security of our elections._He hates it because it works._**
It lets people vote on their schedule — while they’re working, caring for their families, and living their lives. It raises voter turnout by putting a ballot directly into the hands of every voter so everyone has a chance to participate in our democracy.
And that is bad for Trump and his MAGA allies because their policies are wildly unpopular — and voting is how we fight back. Against this administration’s dangerous authoritarian agenda, against ICE, against every cruel attack they throw at our communities.
**_That_ is what they’re afraid of. Our power when we are organized, connected, and showing up at the ballot box in numbers they cannot suppress. **
I will never stop fighting to protect our right to vote. I will continue to stand up against this administration as they try to weaponize our courts, our postal service, and our election system to stay in power.
But I can’t do it alone. The stakes couldn’t be higher, and I need you standing alongside me in this fight.
[**If you’re able, will you please pitch in $3 today or whatever you can to help me keep fighting to protect our rights and defend our democracy?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260906.YKe_7u&refcode=em20260906-6692&amount=3&t=4&akid=6692%2E420207%2Ey2q9Ac)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260906.YKe_7u&amount=3&refcode=em20260906-6692&t=23&akid=6692%2E420207%2Ey2q9Ac)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260906-6692-footer&t=24&refcode2=6692_420207_y2q9Ac&akid=6692%2E420207%2Ey2q9Ac)**

name: OnePA Team
subject: Stand with postal workers this Labor Day
body:
When working people organize, powerful people cannot simply make the rules for everyone else. | |
---
Peter, **Labor Day is about more than a long weekend. It is about the power working people have built by organizing together and refusing to accept a country where the wealthy and powerful get to make all the rules.** That power matters far beyond the workplace. Strong unions give working people a voice. They build leaders in our communities. They create organized power that can stand in the way when politicians try to take rights away from the rest of us. That’s what happened in South Korea, South Africa, Brazil, and across the world when authoritarians tried to silence people. And that is exactly what postal workers are doing right now. **The American Postal Workers Union is standing against a Trump-backed USPS rule that seeks to block mail ballots based on a so-called citizenship verification system built partly with flawed Department of Homeland Security data.** Postmaster General David Steiner finalized the rule even though it is blocked from taking effect for now. He wants the USPS ready to move if the courts give him an opening. **Postal workers and in their union have been clear: their sacred role is to be delivering our ballots, not being forced into a voter suppression scheme.** [**This Labor Day, stand with postal workers and tell the USPS Board of Governors to reverse this rule before it can be used against voters.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38Nq1_jt3eTKpU1jspP0CGWUHXwT4Mj-KsklYkF0f7G6mcjbX0YknbVRgHCRNIxk70U5NuJ2OAB9k8voqq_Em1rimkh2KT2FInv5yN-_31R6dzup5LdXSHNKixpK4iyTC3wMYparpsbSqAAyCGfXbQKikkH79gb3vBUMNl_NjWgaUP7KYWODsYPAKocCkkZkEN2BETTk4M27Cpes8iY9qSsmO3U8SE7Ke5BrH3nEAmRlgc0vGopQnLWO2PCNXveRkF18gY9SvSDG6KOjeqEKPF4iUPxkIt2epY2Pg0_j58_7GEX5Q7tuLAjHcWtlBEak-IRr1RtaET9vX6rhFeyDlMlIV12mZv_hXsK2MjWSSnsWHKpqIdb-Q_VOf-l_ZUD6Gqm1vF6buYXHAtOpZiU5BbGDJBpT8lpj67hch9ioLEtcJ1b0lvzyncgc-N-QzShlHF6gl0HS0hP57HvpYEXx9VjhugFnjiTra9l2Ij3ujtDMfFCSCpFeBfB-ouNxm9VLsI/4tt/6B56HzkaTJuDPvN8t_fkLA/h0/h001.3p5SuL7Tr5Vi9wdOLI4Daa_-Nfu6RaR9yuU8403zYQM) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38Nq1_jt3eTKpU1jspP0CGWUHXwT4Mj-KsklYkF0f7G6mcjbX0YknbVRgHCRNIxk70U5NuJ2OAB9k8voqq_Em1rimkh2KT2FInv5yN-_31R6dzup5LdXSHNKixpK4iyTC3wMYparpsbSqAAyCGfXbQKikkH79gb3vBUMNl_NjWgaUP7KYWODsYPAKocCkkZkEN2BETTk4M27Cpes8iY9qSsmO3U8SE7Ke5BrH3nEAmRlgc0vGopQnLWO2PCNXveRkF18gY9SvSDG6KOjeqEKPF4S0AFSKSoodb2fz4TPi1zLM2b_4nJcytuQmaKdSIPfHnt94ENkOpEnXe__VbuDSxEciVHA9hVS1dYeoE0sqNzRyqg8sjaOv5WCWGEAcIfE1tTIVBmwHSHUP7r1io7fPeR5hpcsXBNlPG6wdn5XdOofRGuOFPFxNQR7HYX7h6xVQBrE5rSrM6UcJkduyV9bxEyVUdV3whCSgsMIKhpVdarD5dELF6zp1x1QS4QxYEr3uk/4tt/6B56HzkaTJuDPvN8t_fkLA/h1/h001.azbR17dc6nOryMBmfN_Cze19xxCqRB7FmvVbBgNJ6vo)
---
**The fight for economic justice and the fight for democracy have always been connected because both come down to power.**
When working people are organized, when Black communities can build political power, and when unions are strong enough to stand together, politicians and wealthy interests cannot simply push us aside. That is why people who want unchecked power work so hard not only to silence voters, and divide our communities, but also to weaken unions.
We ignore economic justice at our own peril. A democracy where people have a vote but no real power in their workplaces, neighborhoods, or government will always leave too much control in the hands of those with the most money and access.
**Generations of workers have shown us another way. We organize. We stand together. We build enough collective power to defend what previous generations won and push our communities forward.**
[**Stand with postal workers this Labor Day and send your message demanding that the Board of Governors stop Trump’s voter suppression scheme.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38Nq1_jt3eTKpU1jspP0CGWUHXwT4Mj-KsklYkF0f7G6mcjbX0YknbVRgHCRNIxk70U5NuJ2OAB9k8voqq_Em1rimkh2KT2FInv5yN-_31R6dzup5LdXSHNKixpK4iyTC3wMYparpsbSqAAyCGfXbQKikkH79gb3vBUMNl_NjWgaUP7KYWODsYPAKocCkkZkEN2BETTk4M27Cpes8iY9qSsmO3U8SE7Ke5BrH3nEAmRlgc0vGopQnLWO2PCNXveRkF18gY9SvSDG6KOjeqEKPF4DwS1dLiq6uqgwmeU_rI4Ecz6NLAce9NzJbCR8q2Tj9QD_2nQSDqkZyym9HTs_kEaamdegjbmnGDTSQNGFy4wFYSHygzLHAT8NdXgG3hlN0u8tVqxoOVI7DyUTInHAcpuBAEChVB5-91aFK11u1hKKR6MFQyR1diGoO6ctBOSdq2SVtMNyL-gzfZYVfGrYybQNa5lOO06FecogypYkXSY_rKp545eMOuc_9UL1WFRM64/4tt/6B56HzkaTJuDPvN8t_fkLA/h2/h001.bzGxPMvVoYBWUEWFTgHMtEUy1ZKuV4Kg_hJov-OKQvg)
Let’s keep building power together,
-OnePA

I’m committed to supporting candidates who will fight corruption in Washington.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41566%2E3422442%2Enc6XOb)
Peter,
A new poll shows that a staggering 89% of U.S. adults think government corruption is widespread—up 10% from last year alone.
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260906_1_ak.ZK2mPB&refcode=em20260906-41566&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41566%2E3422442%2Enc6XOb)
It’s no surprise why: Donald Trump’s administration took corruption to a whole new level. He’s been gifted a $400 million jet from a foreign nation and raked in over a BILLION dollars from cryptocurrency while in office.
Meanwhile, a Congressional stock trading ban _still_ hasn’t passed, allowing members of Congress to trade on insider knowledge while working families suffer.
It’s not enough for Democrats to just call out corruption—we have to end it.
**That’s why I’m supporting candidates who reject corporate PAC money.** Instead of going to Congress to do the bidding of special interests, these candidates are unbought and ready to fight exclusively for working people.
I’m backing leaders ready to take on corruption, but I need your help to make sure they win in November.

Katie Porter

subject: ICE is bypassing our state laws
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
#
Peter,
In March 2023, the Minnesota House of Representatives took a historic stand and moved to ban private prisons in the state — ensuring corporations couldn’t profit off human detention.
But now, _ICE is moving to completely bypass the ban and reopen one anyway._
Early last month, CoreCivic announced they sold the Prairie Correctional Facility in Appleton to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security for a massive $495.6 million.
**A former private prison, this 1,600-bed facility will be used as a privately run ICE detention center as soon as this fall.** Instead of being run by a public safety agency, this prison will be managed by a corporation with little state oversight.
ICE and the Trump administration are trying to make an example out of Minnesota, again. As Minnesota’s Department of Corrections Commissioner Paul Schnell recently put it:
_“Minnesota is once again being forced to absorb the consequences of a reckless and poorly implemented effort that will likely result in more unnecessary deaths, family separations, community outrage, and significant local impacts.”_
This isn’t just about Donald Trump’s immigration force bypassing state law — it’s a direct threat to our neighbors and the communities we love.
Appleton Mayor Justin Koepp and local community leaders have raised major concerns about what this facility means for the town’s infrastructure, services, and long-term vitality. Selling this facility to the federal government creates a massive financial blow to local property tax revenue that Appleton has relied on, **stripping $800,000 away from fixing local roads, funding classrooms, and keeping emergency services staffed.**
Trump and his billionaire megadonors think they can treat rural America like a dumping ground for their worst ideas, expecting small towns to take the hit while corporate executives count their profits.
_We refuse to let them get away with it, Peter._

Thank you,
TimWalz.com

Hi, we have a wild stat to share with you today.

Out of everyone who receives these emails, on average, only 0.002% of people chip in. That’s the truth.

Even more mindblowing is the fact that small-dollar donations like these account for a HUGE portion of our entire grassroots fundraising for the campaign. Support from folks like you – not billionaires and corporate special interests – is the driving force behind this movement, and we’re incredibly proud and grateful.

**But this also means that if you care about winning this race in Ohio and taking back the Senate, we need you to donate today.**

Right now, GOP super PACs and dark-money groups are spending more than $133 million to defeat Sherrod and stop us from flipping this seat – and tech billionaire Peter Thiel recently went live with a $3.6 million ad buy propping up our opponent, Jon Husted.

They all know that Ohio is where the battle for Senate control begins and ends, and if we don’t have the resources to stay competitive, this is a battle we’re going to lose.

Sorry, Hillary. I didn't vote for you.
Solely being a woman isn't a qualification for leadership.
Peter, I've had some stuff on my mind and it feels really good to get it off my chest.
I'm sure you know by now that I've recently walked away from a career I loved. Plenty of people call me crazy for it. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line._
_Especially in my beloved Minnesota.
Right now, parents who speak up are being called transphobes. Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet. And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
It's terrible.
That's why I've taken a huge leap of faith. I want my daughter and every young girl and boy across the country to know this:
1) You earn your place 2) You think for yourself 3) You never let anyone put you in a box
That's exactly what I'm fighting for.
It's not rocket science. GIRLS' sports are for GIRLS.
And if you are to remember one thing about me let it be this: I will not apologize for taking a stand. At the end of the day, if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, I've done my job.
Now, the contingent of people on the radical Left who have been pushing this ideology tirelessly on us will stop at absolutely nothing.
Whether I face Peggy Flanagan or Angie Craig, I'm going up against a far-Left, extremist who will vote to allow boys competing against girls in sports, block voter ID requirements, open up our borders, raise your taxes, and sabotage anything the President wants to do.

I'm far from a career politician. My campaign is focused on honesty, common sense, stopping fraud, and doing the small things right.
That's why we need to win. Failure here is not an option.
And without your help, Peter... we will never cut through the far Left's propaganda machine to get our message out.

My husband and I watched Scranton’s former mayor resign in disgrace after pleading guilty to federal corruption charges, criminal conspiracy, bribery, and attempted extortion.

**August 21, 2019**
I announced my Independent campaign for Scranton mayor and against the local Democratic Party’s cronyism. Our campaign was dubbed _Paige Against the Machine._

**November 5, 2019**
I won our historic mayoral campaign, becoming the first female mayor of Scranton after winning a tough election against the local Democratic machine — all while eight months pregnant.

**January 6, 2020**
Just two weeks after my daughter Sloane was born, I was sworn in as mayor. In the six years since then, we cleaned up City Hall, balanced the books, cut red tape, and brought hundreds of small businesses and over a thousand homes to our neighborhoods.

**September 2, 2025**
We launched this campaign for Congress to challenge corrupt Rob Bresnahan and restore accountability in NEPA. It somehow feels like a lifetime ago and just yesterday.

**May 19, 2026**
We advanced to the general election, and I became the official Democratic nominee to take on Rob and his corruption in November. I’m ready to reform Congress the way I reformed Scranton — but I need your help to do it.

The day we’re going to win this thing and take the next step to move NEPA forward!

| | | I've spent months telling you this administration's efforts to subvert our mail-ballot system was reckless and cynical. A federal whistleblower just proved it.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138702321/644906921/-569431239?refcode=260906-whistleblower-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MTJhYjc1OC0zMmFhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=F1YAAThHSpsO1-ApBsu8jumCGEdi7eUF3kigu7wPmww=)

In a complaint filed with Senator Richard Blumenthal, an anonymous USPS official revealed that the agency built its Trump-ordered ballot-verification system so fast and so carelessly that, in the whistleblower's own words, **"catastrophic failure would be a feature rather than a bug."** Read that again. The system could send a ballot into repeated verification cycles and delay it indefinitely. **Multiply that by every mail voter in Oregon and you get a real possibility: millions of legitimate ballots, stuck,****_undelivered, in November._** Here's the timeline. The Supreme Court cleared a procedural hurdle for this rule on Monday. USPS rushed out its final version by Friday. Oregon and 23 other states sued again within days. A federal court has already slapped a temporary restraining order on most of it. We are winning the legal fights. We've beaten this administration in court twice already. But **winning in court doesn't fix a system that a federal insider says was built to fail.** My office has to be ready for every version of what comes next — a portal that might get forced on us, a rule that might get revived, a scramble to protect 25 years of vote-by-mail no matter what Washington throws at us. **[But I need your help. Can you please chip in just $5 today to help us take the fight to all corners of Oregon? | | | Fellow Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack.

Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God.

For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed.

And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives.

Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for.

He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly.

clean_body: | | | | | | | Fellow Patriot, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. Fellow Patriot, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece. JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like. The dream of almost every immigrant who arrives on our shores is that they will be measured not by their past or their parents' professions but instead by their own ability. And more importantly, perhaps, that the next generation will grow up in a land of opportunity. Indeed, for generations, the goal of most parents (immigrant or not) was for their children to have it better than they did.
The path chosen to achieve this goal was almost always education. Many parents (mine included) prioritized education over almost every other activity. Time and money were dedicated to schooling and support for learning. And more often than not, the system worked. Many children of immigrant households found themselves entering elite schools and finding opportunities their parents never imagined.
I am living proof that it was possible for immigrants to come here, work hard, encourage and prioritize education for their children, and to see their children enjoy better lives. But this bargain rested on an assumption nobody really had to examine, at least not until today. We knew what that an education was valuable, distinguishing, and would retain its worth indefinitely. I am no longer confident in my last sentence.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..maiSPFyF68Gs6e744uSQPH-o_TLC9KIBFCKXqyf7vZc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214339863)
I don't know if there was ever a time when our country was a true meritocracy, but it certainly feels less meritocratic than it used to be. The doors of opportunity appear closed to an increasing number of people. The tip of this spear is college education, which sure seems out of reach for an average family, regardless of how talented their children may be.
The Varsity Blues scandal was perhaps the most shameless example of how far some elites were willing to go to get their kids accepted into an elite college. At least thirty-three parents paid more than $25 million to the mastermind of the scheme, Rick Singer, to secure their children seats at leading colleges. The whole affair revealed what many working-class parents had feared: college admissions were not the even playing fields they presented as being. It was also, in retrospect, the amateur version. Bribery is what you resort to when you lack a better instrument.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/02e438c1-9541-4058-a671-e4f73bb5739b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But perhaps the surest path to an elite education is to attend one of the feeder high schools that act as a pipeline to top colleges. Under 1% of applicants from a typical public high school get accepted at Ivy-plus universities. The number can be in the 20%-30% range for the country's most elite private schools. These top feeders place 25 to 40 times more students at elite colleges than the national baseline. Of course, these schools are exorbitantly expensive, with tuition often running north of $60,000 per year. At least that $60,000 is paid openly, and paid by the family that benefits.
The parents of Lexington, Massachusetts may have found the best way to game the system yet: build their own feeder school...and even better, with taxpayer dollars. Lexington High School is already one of the top public feeder schools in the Greater Boston area, sending graduates to Harvard, MIT, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania. It's ranked fifth in Massachusetts and 167th nationally by U.S. News. And last year, the parents of Lexington decided to take things a step further.
In December 2025, voters approved a $660 million project to tear down their 70-year-old high school and build a brand-new one. The school will be one of the most expensive public school construction projects in American history. (It's noteworthy that the project budget was made before the Iran war led to widespread inflationary pressure, so the actual number may be significantly higher). The "Bloom" design features 440,000 square feet, an 800-seat dining center, a grab-and-go cafe, an enclosed courtyard, and a fully renovated field house. The state is even picking up a share of the cost, kicking in $121 million; Lexington taxpayers are carrying the remaining $533 million, financed through 30-year bonds. The cost per square foot ($1,293) works out to roughly $275,000 per kid.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e74951c6-624c-4c5b-9bd7-6eb971bbcc2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's be precise about what makes this work, because the obvious objection is that Lexington High is a public school open to anyone. That is true and the admission requirement is simply for the child to be living in a house in Lexington. The tuition is real, even if it is paid as a mortgage rather than to a bursar. It also happens to be partly deductible and much of it is recoverable at resale. It is the most elegant private-school payment plan ever devised.
And then there is the $121 million from the state. Lexington's average household income is $281,187. Whatever the state money is, it is not need-based aid. It is the rest of Massachusetts helping one of its wealthiest towns preserve a competitive advantage over the rest of Massachusetts.
Let me concede a fair defense before making my point. The $275,000-per-student figure is a capital cost spread against a building meant to last forty years or more; amortized, it is a few thousand dollars a year per student, which is not by itself a scandalous number. Buildings do wear out, and the Lexington High School was seventy years old.
The number that actually matters and recurs is the debt service, the least flexible line in a municipal budget. It cannot be trimmed in a bad year. It comes ahead of teacher salaries, ahead of curriculum, and ahead of new priorities that might emerge in 2038. Lexington has not merely spent $660 million. It has pre-committed three decades of its education budget to a single decision made in a single December.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..maiSPFyF68Gs6e744uSQPH-o_TLC9KIBFCKXqyf7vZc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214339863)
This is a wealthy community socializing the cost of maintaining its own advantage, and doing it more skillfully than Rick Singer ever managed or imagined. But it is not the most interesting thing about the deal. The most interesting thing is that it may not actually work.
A thirty-year bond is a thirty-year bet on the value of the thing it finances. Lexington's bondholders are protected either way; they hold a claim on the town's tax base, not on its results. The families are not protected. What they have actually bought is not 440,000 square feet of dining center and field house. It is a potential improvement in the odds of admission to a small number of institutions. That is a positional good, and a positional good is worth exactly what the position is worth when the bill comes due.
**And nobody knows what that position will be worth in 2056.** A hundred years ago an educated man was someone who spoke and wrote Latin and Greek. That was not a foolish standard. It was a reasonable proxy for a mind trained to do hard things, and it held for centuries -- until it stopped holding, quite quickly. Every credential is a proxy, and proxies decay when the thing underneath them changes. What does it mean to be educated in the 21st century? How will artificial intelligence impact the value of whatever our children are taught?
Nobody at the town meeting knew, and I don't hold it against them. Nobody anywhere knows. But that uncertainty is precisely the argument for spending flexibly and reversibly on teachers, on curriculum, on things that can be changed in five years. A thirty-year general obligation bond is the least reversible instrument a town owns. Lexington answered a question about the future by pouring concrete. Worse, a recent budget shortfall had them actually cutting teachers and staff while they plan a $660 million expenditure. So the town is _**actually cutting education resources**_ _**that will certainly impact students immediately**_ to finance buildings with _**uncertain**_ value to students. Why not make education about....well...education?
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e278b779-05fe-4317-8f83-581cafe003fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The anecdotal conversation I'm hearing is all about status, bragging rights, and the ability to someday wear the "MIT Parent" sweatshirt. Now don't get me wrong, I'm not opposed to elite education. I'm both a product and a fan of it. But I also know it's not for everyone. In today's dynamic economy, the purpose and value of an elite education is unclear. It's not zero, as some suggest. But it's also not a sure-fire way to be profiled on "The Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous."
Increasingly, and I would argue usefully, education is about the student and their ability to take advantage of the opportunities they encounter. For many, this may mean acquiring a trade skill and starting their own electric, plumbing, or HVAC service company. For others, it may mean acquiring nursing or other medical skills to meet the needs of an aging population. Those are not consolation prizes. They are bets on demand we can actually see from here, which is more than can be said for the one Lexington just made.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..maiSPFyF68Gs6e744uSQPH-o_TLC9KIBFCKXqyf7vZc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214339863)
Most decisions we make in today's world involve tradeoffs. And while there's no reason a community shouldn't feel at liberty to spend two thirds of a billion dollars on a high school, it would be naive to think it didn't imply a set of values. A budget is a statement of belief, and Lexington's says the binding constraint on its children's success is the building. I doubt that. The constraint is that no one in that room (or in any comparable room in the country) can say with confidence what an educated person will need to know in twenty years.
My parents had no field house to offer me. What they had was a conviction about what mattered and the discipline to act on it, and that conviction cost nothing per square foot. Lexington's children will graduate from the most expensive public high school ever built in America. The last coupon on that bond comes due in 2056, and only then will we know whether the credential it was meant to secure was worth securing. The bondholders don't have to answer that question. The children of recent graduates do.

**Dear Peter,**
| _**Take a deep breath.**_ **I know the news is unsettling.**
---
It feels like every day the radical establishment gives us a new reason to worry about our families, our values, and our country’s future. But I’m writing to tell you something important:

**Team:** Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. **That's no longer the case.** Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a _regional processing facility_ , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. **How does this impact vote-by-mail?** If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- _something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those_ \-- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, _a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day,_ making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. **Of course, this was followed by the recent news that USPS won't deliver your ballot unless your state put your name on Trump's list** \-- usurping the Constitution and trying to take control of elections away from the states in order to suppress the vote. **[Team, Every voter needs to know about these massive changes. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those \-- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

**China 's Two-Front Play: Buying America's Land -- and Its Narrative**
Taken together, investigative reporter Natalie Winters' two latest Substack exclusives describe what she presents as a two-front campaign by Chinese interests inside the United States: hard assets near a critical military installation, and soft power inside the American press.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/32343120-366e-49f2-864c-ac956c1d6a29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**A Secret Buyer Near the Navy 's Fighter-Jet Hub**
A corporation the U.S. Department of Agriculture classifies as Chinese-owned paid $21.2 million in cash for more than 1,500 acres of California farmland roughly 16 miles from Naval Air Station Lemoore -- the Navy's principal West Coast fighter-jet base -- according to federal and county records cited in Winters' report. USDA's AFIDA filings dated December 31, 2024, show Long Feng International, Inc., listed under China, holding 1,513 acres in Kings County near Corcoran: prime pistachio ground in the Central Valley.
The red flag, she argues, is anonymity. No individual owner is publicly attached to the company, which is why she labels it "potentially CCP-linked" even as USDA paperwork lists it under China.
**The Americans on China 's Payroll**
Her second report names dozens of prominent U.S. journalists and commentators who took all-expenses-paid delegations to China sponsored by the China-United States Exchange Foundation (CUSEF), a Hong Kong-based group she documents as CCP-linked and registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act. Drawing on FARA filings, CUSEF's own publications, and internal reports, Winters argues the trips were engineered to generate "favorable coverage" and "positive messages" for Beijing -- with organizers controlling the itineraries, lodging, and access.
Among those named: The Atlantic's Clive Crook, WNYC's Brian Lehrer, the Chicago Tribune's Steve Chapman, U.S. News & World Report's Tom Omestad, and Bruce Stokes, with outlets cited including The New York Times, CNN, and Vox. A 2012 internal report touting a $60,000 delegation bragged that participants returned with "shifted views" on China and plans to adjust their coverage. Winters also notes that then-Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns headlined some CUSEF events during his tenure.
**The Common Thread**
Winters' throughline is opacity. Whether it's $21.2 million in cash for farmland in the shadow of a fighter-jet hub, or sponsored junkets that mature into media influence, she argues Beijing's playbook depends on transactions Americans never see -- shell companies with no named owners, and "exchange" groups whose lobbying filings tell a different story. Her closing warning: U.S. safeguards, from foreign-ownership disclosure to land-purchase restrictions near military bases, haven't kept pace with either front.
\---
*Sources: nataliegwinters.substack.com -- "EXC: Secret Chinese Buyer Purchased Farmland Near U.S. Navy's Pacific Fighter Jet Hub" and "EXC: Exposed: How Americans on China's Payroll."*

Texas is a big state. **In fact, Texas has more counties than any other state in the country.**
With 254 counties, from the Panhandle to the Rio Grande Valley, East Texas to the Hill Country, every community has its own story, its own challenges, and its own vision for the future.
But too many Texans have been left behind by Greg Abbott’s leadership.

clean_body: The noise is a distraction from our mission. | | Dear Peter, | Take a deep breath. I know the news is unsettling. It feels like every day the radical establishment gives us a new reason to worry about our families, our values, and our country’s future. But I’m writing to tell you something important: | It is going to be okay. | We don't need more out-of-touch elites yelling at us from their ivory towers. We need a return to the fundamentals that made this country great: | ★ | Rewarding hard work and personal responsibility. ---|--- ★ | Restoring law and order to our streets. ★ | Protecting a future where our children are taught, not indoctrinated. This isn't just "politics as usual." It’s about reclaiming our common sense. | The noise is designed to keep us divided and distracted. The truth is that we want a country that is safe, solvent, and free. We are finding our way back to our core values — and I want you to stand with us on this path. | Thank you, — Steve Hilton Authorized by Steve Hilton for Governor 2026 If you would like to opt-out of important updates like this,

U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) is once again thanking President Donald Trump for making the decision to move the U.S. Space Command Headquarters to Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville.

It was a year ago when Trump made the announcement in the Oval Office. U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) wants to protect high school football, and the community it creates for Alabamians, on Friday nights from a potential media grab from college football.

The Protect College Sports Act (PCSA), which is currently making its way through Congress, has a provision that says schools can join a voluntary collective to pool and jointly negotiate their media rights.

Britt wants to ensure this doesn’t affect the high school football schedule.

Alabama’s soon-to-be-senior U.S. Senator, who is a huge fan of the game, discussed the bill recently on Alabama Public Television’s “Capitol Journal.”

“I want to make sure that we protect Friday night lights,” Britt said.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83407040-0d05-40c6-8f26-4c542050cb4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I was thirteen, standing on a bimah in a sanctuary that smelled like candle wax and old prayer books, singing my Torah portion badly and meaning it completely. Bar mitzvah, 1980s America. The room wasn't all Jewish -- my Little League coach was there, our Methodist neighbors, my father's boss. When the scroll was lifted, the whole room stood. We had agreed on something back then: a Jewish kid claiming his place in an ancient covenant was a beautiful, American thing. Respect wasn't a hashtag. It was a folding chair and a Gentile coach saying *mazel tov* with a Kansas accent.
This week I read a piece that took me back to that room -- then showed me how far we've fallen.
"The Rise of Youth Antisemitism," at a Substack called The Hill of Spring, is by Leo Lewis, a New York high schooler. He goes to school, in his words, with "the future leaders of America," and he is sounding the alarm on them. The sentence I can't shake: the word antisemitism has been "almost completely defanged. Being called antisemitic is itself a joke."
Read that again. In my bar mitzvah decade, an antisemite was the one thing nobody wanted to be. When neo-Nazis tried to march through Skokie in the seventies, the whole country looked at them like something you scrape off your shoe. The hatred existed -- it always exists -- but it hid. It whispered.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a9a7524-6a1a-4734-9331-c453b067031f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Today it streams. Lewis's diagnosis is surgical: a strain of antisemitism built from conspiracy theories, jokes, and social media, spreading fastest among young men. Memes, streamers, podcast provocateurs, Holocaust punchlines passed like trading cards. And the data agrees with the hallway: a national survey this year found the youngest adult generations now top the chart in belief of classic antisemitic tropes -- raised after the museums were built, most likely to believe the blood libels.
The arrow is pointing backwards.
Lewis doesn't just diagnose the hate; he diagnoses the vacuum: loneliness, civic decay, lost confidence in America. When a young man loses faith in every institution, the algorithm hands him the oldest product in the world: a hidden truth, and a person to blame. And the jokes are the anesthesia -- you laugh ironically, but nobody ever laughed his way into the light. The joke is the door. The hate walks in later, in its socks.
I write this as someone who found Yeshua -- Jesus -- as an adult and was born again. Nobody warned me I'd become more Jewish, not less. Or as my Australian Christian friend who runs Nashville's The Cookery says, 'doubly blessed'. My Bible is a Jewish book. My Lord said, "Salvation is from the Jews," and Paul wrote to Gentile believers: "Do not boast over those branches... you do not support the root; the root supports you." If salvation is from the Jews, contempt for Jews cannot be Christianity. It's a wolf in Sunday clothes.
To my Jewish friends: I know what it feels like to lose something you thought was settled, and I mourn it with you. But you were never respected because you were safe; you were respected because we kept a covenant -- and covenants can be rebuilt.
So: don't laugh at the joke. Teach the children what the hatred sounded like. And if you name the Name, bless the people He came from -- loudly. Genesis 12:3 is still in force.
Never again is not a Jewish slogan. It's an American vow.
